title: Global indexing and namespace mapping notes
content:
Purpose and context

This note captures a compact proposal for a canonical global resource index and namespace mapping layer in the control plane. Goals: make CRUD semantics predictable across regions, provide stable canonical IDs, enable lightweight routing policies (region affinity, hard bind, failover), and allow safe schema evolution and migration. It is intentionally pragmatic — we prioritize runtime simplicity for runtime routing and for customer-facing APIs.

Primary requirements (summary)
- Resources must be addressable by a single stable canonical identifier (GUID) independent of region/cluster.
- Support per-account and per-tenant namespaces without global name collisions.
- CRUD APIs must be idempotent and versioned; safe for multi-master replication across regions.
- Routing policies should be expressible as declarative attributes on resources and as separate policy objects.
- Allow cheap regional copies/replicas and explicit single-owner bindings (for Dedicated/Private deployments).
- Low-latency path for common read operations; eventual consistency OK for non-critical metadata.

Concepts and definitions
- canonical_id: immutable global GUID assigned at first create. primary key for control plane record.
- local_handle: human-friendly name that is namespaced by account/org and is unique within that namespace; resolves to canonical_id.
- allocation_bind: optional binding object that pins a canonical_id to a (region, cluster, pool) tuple for serving.
- placement_policy: policy object describing routing hints (preferred_regions, min_capacity, latency_budget_ms, fallback_sequence).
- policy_version: small integer bumped when semantics of a placement_policy change.

ID strategy
- canonical_id = UUIDv4 (128-bit). No embedded region or tenant info to allow movement and rebinding.
- local_handle = <org_id>::<namespace>::<short-name> (string). Stored with a case-insensitive unique index scoped to org_id.
- allocation_bind stores canonical_id -> region(s) + cluster id(s) + timestamp + owner.

Control plane record schema (flat view, important fields)
- canonical_id: string (GUID)
- owner_org: string
- local_handle: string (optional)
- resource_type: string (e.g., model, deployment, route)
- created_at: ISO date string
- updated_at: ISO date string
- desired_state: string (ACTIVE, DELETING, ARCHIVED)
- placement_policy_id: string (nullable)
- current_allocations: comma-separated region:cluster entries (string)
- version: integer (optimistic concurrency token)
- metadata: short json blob as string (must remain < 4KB)

Design rationale: keep the control plane record small so reads are fast; heavy metadata lives in external blob store and is loaded on demand.

CRUD API contract (coarse)
All endpoints live under /api/v1/control/resources. Every write requires an Idempotency-Key header. Responses include canonical_id and version.

- POST /api/v1/control/resources
  - Purpose: create resource (assign canonical_id)
  - Body: {local_handle?, resource_type, owner_org, placement_policy_id?, metadata?}
  - Success: 201 {canonical_id, version, created_at}
  - Error cases: 409 if local_handle already exists in the org namespace
  - Notes: POST is create-only. If caller supplies local_handle that already exists and they want upsert, use PUT /{local_handle} endpoint.

- PUT /api/v1/control/resources/{canonical_id}
  - Purpose: full replace or upsert by canonical_id
  - Body: full record payload; must include version for optimistic concurrency
  - Success: 200 {canonical_id, version}
  - Error: 409 if version mismatch, 404 if canonical_id not found (unless upsert flag provided)

- PUT /api/v1/control/namespaces/{org_id}/resources/{local_handle}
  - Purpose: idempotent create-or-update by handle within namespace. Returns canonical_id.
  - This endpoint implements the common SDK path where customers refer to human names.

- GET /api/v1/control/resources/{canonical_id}
  - Purpose: canonical read for control plane agents. Returns full summary record (not heavy metadata blob).
  - Query flags: ?include_metadata=true|false

- GET /api/v1/control/namespaces/{org_id}/resources/{local_handle}
  - Purpose: resolve local_handle -> canonical_id + minimal record

- PATCH /api/v1/control/resources/{canonical_id}
  - Purpose: partial update (e.g., placement_policy_id, desired_state)
  - Body: partial fields + version
  - Success: 200 with new version

- DELETE /api/v1/control/resources/{canonical_id}
  - Purpose: mark desired_state=DELETING and enqueue async cleanup
  - Returns 202 accepted with job id

API semantics and strong vs eventual consistency
- Strong consistency is required for handle uniqueness checks and for ownership transfers. These operations use a single-shard leader lease and synchronous writes.
- Most updates to placement hints and metadata are eventual; they propagate via async replication (changefeed).
- Reads: control plane supports a read-from-nearest replica mode for low-latency reads; callers can request strong read if they need the latest version.

Routing policy language (short)
- Placement policy is a small declarative object: {id, preferred_regions:[], hard_bind?: boolean, fallback_sequence:[], capacity_guardrails:{min_instances, max_instances}, latency_budget_ms}
- Semantics:
  - hard_bind=true means allocation_bind(s) are authoritative; routing must only consider those allocations.
  - preferred_regions is a ranked list of regions; scheduler tries them in order when allocating.
  - fallback_sequence lists region(s) to try after preferred_regions are exhausted.
  - latency_budget_ms is used to avoid routing to regions that are likely to exceed SLOs.

Allocation lifecycle and bindings
- Allocation is created by the scheduler and stored as an allocation_bind record: {canonical_id, region, cluster, pool, status, created_at, owner, version}
- Allocation status: ALLOCATED | UNHEALTHY | DRAINING | RELEASED
- Rebinding path (for Dedicated migrations): user triggers Rebind API -> control plane writes a new allocation_bind with status ALLOCATED and then transitions the previous bind to DRAINING -> RELEASED once healthy.

Multi-region replication and conflict policy
- For high-traffic objects (routes, short-lived deployments), we allow multi-master writes for non-conflicting fields (e.g., metrics counters). For canonical metadata we prefer single-writer per canonical_id: the control-plane shard leader for the canonical_id acts as authoritative writer. Writes routed to non-leader are proxied or redirected.
- Conflict detection: optimistic versioning (version integer). On conflict, client receives 409 and should re-read and retry the change with new version.

Idempotency and retries
- All mutating endpoints require Idempotency-Key to protect from duplicate retries. The control plane persists Idempotency-Key -> response mapping for 24 hours.

Edge cases and migration notes
- Moving a resource between orgs: disallowed. Owner org is immutable to avoid permission complexity. To change ownership create a new resource and deprecate the old one.
- Renaming local_handle: allowed, must maintain history mapping for 30 days to support cached references. Renaming is an atomic operation that checks for uniqueness in the target namespace.
- Emergency failover: an operator can call /rebind/{canonical_id}?force=true to set ALLOCATED in a target region and mark previous allocations DRAINING. This bypasses placement checks and must be audited.

Operational considerations
- Backing store: distributed transactional DB sharded by canonical_id prefix. Global index for local_handle -> canonical_id uses strongly-consistent single-shard writes.
- Changefeed: every write emits a change event consumed by scheduler and edge routers. Use topic partitioning by canonical_id for ordering.
- Metrics: record per-write latency, index conflict rate, rebind frequency, avg time to allocate, and percent reads served by nearest replica.
- Quotas and rate limits: namespace-level create rate limit to avoid handle-squatting storms.

Versioning and forward compatibility
- API v1 minimum fields as above. Additive changes only for v1.*; breaking changes must go to v2 and support dual-writing period.
- placement_policy uses small policy_version integer to allow routers/schedulers to advance semantics without changing canonical record schema.

Open questions / discussion items
- Should canonical_id embed tenant hint to optimize sharding for hot orgs? (tradeoff: harder to move between shards).
- Replica read consistency defaults: nearest replica vs leader read — what should SDK default be?
- How long should we keep rename history? 30 days suggested but ops may want longer for long-lived caches.
- Approach for soft deletes vs hard deletes and long retention requirements for audits.

Next steps / action items
- Align with SRE on expected read QPS patterns and choose sharding prefix strategy. (Owner: Ravi)
- Draft a migration playbook for Dedicated -> Hosted resource rebinding. (Owner: Tanya)
- Prototype local_handle uniqueness enforcement using leader-lease per namespace and measure latency. (Owner: Eric)

Appendix: sample flow - create + allocate + route
1) Client POST /resources {local_handle: "acme::default::translate-route", owner_org: "acme", resource_type: "route", placement_policy_id: "pp-1"}
2) Control plane returns canonical_id C1 and version 1.
3) Scheduler consumes changefeed, evaluates placement_policy pp-1 and creates allocation_bind C1 -> us-west-2:cluster-17 (status ALLOCATED).
4) Router queries GET /namespaces/acme/resources/translate-route -> gets canonical_id C1 and current_allocations; uses nearest allocated cluster for routing.

This note is intentionally compact — follow-ups will expand specific API payload models and include sequence diagrams for leader routing and cross-region replication.
